title: R’ Nachum, R’ Abbahu’s attendant
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Yevamot 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.42b.10), R’ Abbahu went along leaning on the shoulder of R’ Nachum, his attendant; he went along eliciting halakhah from him. He asked him, ‘A dispute followed by an anonymous teaching—what is the ruling?’ etc.

Hyman says it is possible that he is R’ Nachum mentioned in [Berakhot, chapter 4, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.4.3.15): R’ Zeira sent to R’ Nachum regarding R’ Yannai son of R’ Yishmael, etc.

In [Berakhot, chapter 9, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.2.20), and [Taanit, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.1.3.3), R’ Nachum, R’ Chizkiyah and R’ Ada bar Bimi (Taanit reads bar Ivuma) were sitting. R’ Nachum (Hyman says Berakhot mistakenly reads R’ Tanchum) said to R’ Abba bar Avimi, ‘Does it not make sense that this was said about the blessing?’ etc.
And in [Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.1.9.3): Rabbi Nachum said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Abba.
And in [Bava Batra, beginning of chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.4.1.2): Nachum in the name of R’ Chiya bar Abba.

notes.text: In Yevamot, shammaya means attendant. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yevamot.42b.10.1) explains mankit as gathering settled rulings. The compressed wording in Hyman’s notice leaves the actor of the following clause unstated.

In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:3, Rabbi Zeira sends to Rabbi Nachum concerning Yannai son of Yishmael. Hyman suggests that this may be the same Nachum. The consulted Berakhot 9:2 reads bracketed Nachum and Rav Ada bar Avimi, and the parallel Taanit Hebrew reads Ada bar Ikhuma. Hyman reports and discusses Bimi, Ivuma, Tanchum and Abba bar Avimi.

Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:9 preserves Nachum’s report of Shmuel bar Abba’s question. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 922) appears to give ה״ט where the supplied transcription has ה״מ. Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 4:1 gives the final transmission as Rabbi Nachum in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba.
